extracted.intended_audience: newsrooms, broadcast and digital journalists submitting to the RTDNA Edward R. Murrow Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and category definitions for preparing and submitting local or national news work to the Edward R. Murrow Awards, including time limits, category constraints, and the program's core evaluation pillars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to RTDNA Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize local and national news stories that uphold the RTDNA Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the three pillars for evaluation; entries should demonstrate ethical journalistic behavior consistent with the RTDNA Code of Ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical expertise (production craft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate technical expertise and production craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second of the three pillars; judges evaluate production quality, technical execution, and craft in audio/video/newsgathering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance and impact as community service
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemplify the importance and impact of journalism as a service to the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third pillar; entries should show service to the community, public benefit, and measurable or clear impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: 40 minutes of past-year coverage plus a full newscast
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit 40 minutes of work from the past year along with a complete newscast; this category evaluates overall newsroom excellence across coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newscast
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry is a single regularly scheduled newscast; judged on overall quality, content selection, pacing and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 20 minutes covering a single unscheduled event
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should focus on a single unscheduled breaking event and fit within the 20-minute maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 30 minutes following a major developing story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should present follow-up reporting on a major developing story, demonstrating persistence and depth within a 30-minute limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 10 minutes of human-interest or profile (not breaking, not investigative)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature pieces should be human-interest or profile stories and explicitly are not qualifying as breaking or investigative reporting; 10-minute maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 15 minutes of journalistic enterprise on an important issue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative entries should demonstrate enterprise reporting that uncovers important issues, with a 15-minute maximum for entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard News
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry is one hard news story; judged on timeliness, sourcing, clarity, and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Series
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category for multi-part series; judges will assess cohesion, depth across installments, and cumulative impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Documentary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-form documentary-style reporting category; evaluated for reporting depth, storytelling, accuracy and production values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports Reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers sports journalism entries; assessed for reporting, context, storytelling and production/craft appropriate to sports coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Video / Audio
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category evaluates effective and creative use of video or audio elements in storytelling and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses quality of journalistic writing — clarity, structure, sourcing, and appropriateness for the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Innovation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes innovative approaches to journalism — new forms, technologies, workflows or storytelling methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Social Media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates effective, ethical and impactful use of social media platforms for reporting, engagement, distribution or audience service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Diversity, Equity and Inclusion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes work that brings attention to issues of inequality and demonstrates inclusive reporting practices and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital category
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence in Web Site / Digital Journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards excellence in digital storytelling, website presentation, multimedia integration and online audience service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to community (impact)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit evaluative dimension: judges consider how the reporting serves the public, leads to community benefit or produces measurable impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/craft quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit dimension covering production values, editing, audio/video quality, and professionalism of presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit dimension tied to adherence to RTDNA Code of Ethics; includes fairness, sourcing, transparency and avoidance of conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly valued: novel storytelling forms, platform-specific experimentation, and creative use of technology or format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion of perspectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly valued: inclusion of diverse voices, attention to equity and representation in sourcing and storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence (continuing coverage)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly valued: demonstrated ongoing reporting and follow-up over time on developing stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit dimension: the importance or public relevance of the issue covered is a key consideration for judges.
